task: Horizon 15 of agentic-dataops: The six Assistant skills shipped by adops init: SKILL.md skills that check prerequisites, do the Git work themselves (branch, commit, open a PR, including the PR that carries an accepted-change record), use the MCP tools (run, preview, validate, edit, read-logs, test-connection, accept-schema, drop-branch) and explain each step in plain words

analysis.objective: Make `adops init` and `adops init --demo` write six Claude Code Skills (adops-setup, adops-build, adops-test-in-dev, adops-share, adops-breaking-change, adops-promote) to `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in the user's Project. The Skills let the user's Assistant check Prerequisites, do the Git work itself (branch, commit, push, and a Pull Request, including the one that carries an accepted-change record), call only the existing adops MCP tools in dev and Branch Environments, and explain each step in plain words. This delivers vision item 8 and the skills half of vision item 1.
analysis.successDefinition: Done and correct when ALL of these hold. (1) The demo and plain templates ship exactly six files, `.claude/skills/{adops-setup,adops-build,adops-test-in-dev,adops-share,adops-breaking-change,adops-promote}/SKILL.md`. `adops init` and `adops init --demo` write all six into the new Project, and no tool code is copied. The CI step that checks templates ship in the wheel lists all 12 new template paths. (2) Each SKILL.md has valid YAML front matter: `name` equals its folder name, and `description` is non-empty and says when to use the Skill. (3) Each Skill covers its confirmed scope. adops-setup checks that Docker is installed and running, the compose ports are free, `.env` is filled from `.env.example`, and git and gh are installed and logged in, then starts `docker compose up`. adops-build uses list_files, read_file, project_view, edit_file and validate. adops-test-in-dev uses run, preview, read_logs and test_connection, and explains failures plainly. adops-share creates a branch, commits, pushes, opens a Pull Request with `gh pr create`, and runs the Branch Environment with run/preview `branch=`. adops-breaking-change calls accept_schema in dev, then commits the file at the returned `record_path` under `pipelines/accepted/` on a branch and opens the Pull Request that carries the record. adops-promote, after the merge, calls drop_branch and explains that a merge goes to stage and a release goes to prod. (4) Unit tests, at the repo's 100% line+branch coverage, assert for every Skill that the front matter is valid, that every MCP tool name it mentions is a tool `build_server` really registers (run, preview, validate, drop_branch, accept_schema, project_view, list_files, read_file, edit_file, read_logs, test_connection), and that it never targets stage or prod: no MCP call or adops command passes environment/--env stage or prod, and no Skill runs `adops run --all`, a release or a prod workflow. (5) One E2E test, with no LLM, replays the Git steps of adops-share and adops-breaking-change on a demo Project: git init, create a branch, run dev accept_schema (or a prepared record) to produce `pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml`, commit it, and push to a local bare repo. It asserts the pushed branch holds the record and passes `adops validate`. (6) All existing repo gates stay green: lint, types, 100% coverage, unit job and Docker E2E inside the 20-minute CI budget. No test needs an LLM key.
assumptions: Claude Code finds Project Skills at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, with YAML front matter holding at least `name` and `description`. No other Assistant format ships in v1 (user answer 2, matching the horizon-9 decision to ship .mcp.json only).

The MCP server is named `adops` in `.mcp.json`, so Claude Code shows its tools as `mcp__adops__<tool>`. Skills name tools by their registered Python names (underscores, e.g. accept_schema, read_logs, test_connection, drop_branch). The user's hyphenated names (read-logs, test-connection) map 1:1 to these.

Skills are static Markdown template files copied by the existing `_copy_tree` in init_command.py. No version marker substitution is needed. Dot-folders already ship in the wheel, as `.mcp.json` and `.env.example` show, but the CI template wheel-listing guard (ci.yml:39-56) must be extended.

`adops init` does not run `git init` or create a GitHub repository. adops-setup runs `git init` when the folder is not a repo. adops-share creates the GitHub remote with `gh repo create` when none exists, after asking the user. These steps are the Skills' Git work under ADR-0011.

Both the plain and demo templates get the same six Skills. In a plain Project with no dbt project yet (MAP candidate #17), adops-build covers Pipeline YAML fully and dbt models only where `dbt/` exists.

The 'never targets stage/prod' test is a text rule over each SKILL.md. Skills may mention stage and prod in explanation (adops-promote must explain merge→stage and release→prod). They must never tell the Assistant to call a tool or command with stage or prod. The MCP server's own allow-list refusal stays the real security boundary.
Running a real Assistant over the Skills is not tested (user answer 3). Correctness of the Skill prose is checked by the structural unit tests plus the one Git-replay E2E.
The E2E pushes to a local bare repository and never calls GitHub or gh. The `gh pr create` step is out of the E2E by design.
Horizon 14 (accept_schema returns record_path and writes the dev record) is landed and committed (commit 4d7b6a8).
confirmed: the six Skills are adops-setup, adops-build, adops-test-in-dev, adops-share, adops-breaking-change, adops-promote (user, 2026-11-23)
confirmed: quality bar = structural unit tests on Skill files + one Git replay test (user)
confirmed A1: the Git replay is a Docker-free test in tests/unit with a hand-written record; the Docker E2E already covers real dev accept-schema (user, Stage 3.4)
confirmed A2: Skills name tools as backticked mcp__adops__<tool>; the test reads the tool list from build_server
confirmed A3: plain and demo SKILL.md files are byte-identical and read adops.yaml/.env.example at run time
confirmed A4: share/promote stop and explain when adops.yaml has no stage Environment (plain Project)
confirmed A5: no new ADR; GLOSSARY gets a Skill entry
risks: The stage/prod text rule may give false positives or false negatives. A naive grep for 'stage'/'prod' fails adops-promote, which must explain them. A rule that is too loose misses a disguised instruction. The test must target call and command patterns (environment=, --env, run --all, gh release), and that pattern list must be reviewed.

Tool-name drift: Skills must name the tools that `build_server` registers today. If the test reads names from prose with a regex, wording such as 'read-logs' versus 'read_logs' can let a wrong name slip through or fail a correct one. One canonical form (backticked tool names) has to be chosen and enforced.

Claude Code's real MCP tool-call timeout against long dev and Branch runs is still an open question (h09). The Skills cannot fix it. adops-test-in-dev and adops-share should tell the user a long run may time out and point them to read_logs. Answering the question is MAP #18's job.

Committing the record: accept_schema creates a timestamped file under `pipelines/accepted/`. If the Skill commits on main or forgets to branch first, the record reaches stage without review, which conflicts with ADR-0015. The Skill must create the branch before committing.

Secret leakage through Git: adops-share must never `git add` `.env` or `.adops/`. The plain and demo gitignores cover both, but a Skill using `git add -A` in a Project with an edited or missing .gitignore could commit secrets, against vision item 6. Skills should stage named paths (pipelines/, dbt/, adops.yaml) or check git status first.
Plain-Project gaps: the plain template has no dbt project and no pipelines/accepted folder. Skills written against the demo layout may give wrong instructions in a plain Project.

The Docker E2E budget is 20 minutes and must not be raised (h4 decision). A Git-replay E2E that runs a dev Sync to produce a real Breaking Change adds time. Using a hand-written record checked by `adops validate`, or reusing the existing demo E2E fixture, keeps the cost low.
Users who ran `adops init` before this horizon get no Skills, because init refuses a non-empty folder. There is no upgrade path, the same gap as the h12 server files.
A Branch Environment run needs stage's Warehouse Secret Reference in the local .env (h09 decision). The adops-share Skill must explain this, or users will hit the sanitized error with no context.
outOfScope: Running or evaluating a real Assistant (Claude Code or any LLM) against the Skills: v1 needs no LLM key (vision item 12), and the user set the quality bar to structural tests plus one Git-replay E2E.
Skills for other Assistants (AGENTS.md, Cursor rules, Codex): the user confirmed Claude Code only, consistent with the horizon-9 .mcp.json-only decision.
New or changed MCP tools, including any Git tool inside the MCP server: the horizon-9 decision keeps Git out of the server, so the Skills do Git through the Assistant's shell.

Running stage or prod, `adops run --all`, publishing releases or triggering Promotion workflows from a Skill: ADR-0014 and the horizon-9 allow-list keep the Assistant in dev and Branch Environments. adops-promote only explains this.
Proving Promotion on a real self-hosted runner, or changing the generated GitHub Actions workflows: that is MAP candidate #16.
Adding a dbt project to the plain template: that is MAP candidate #17. Skills only work with whatever dbt/ exists.
Fixing the MCP tool-call timeout for long runs and the `dbt/profiles.yml` dev-redirect gap: that is MAP candidate #18, whose timeout half needs real use of these Skills first.
Calling GitHub or gh in tests (real PR creation, gh auth): tests must stay offline and deterministic, so the E2E stops at a push to a local bare repo.
Automating drop-branch on PR merge or close in CI: horizon 6 made drop-branch manual, and adops-promote calls the MCP drop_branch tool by hand.
An upgrade command that adds Skills to existing Projects: init refuses non-empty folders, and an upgrade path is new CLI surface that nobody requested.
Environments/Promotion and single-VM playbooks: those are vision item 11 and MAP #19. The Skills explain steps inline but are not the playbooks.
An analytics `/ask` Skill: ADR-0010 defers the Analytics Agent and its skill to v1.1.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The Skills encode DataOps workflow rules that a data-engineering expert would recognize: a Breaking Change is accepted only through a reviewed accepted-change record, the Assistant acts only in dev and Branch Environments, and Promotion runs merge→stage and release→prod through Git. The Markdown and test machinery only carries these rules.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A SKILL.md file that `adops init` writes to `.claude/skills/<name>/`, telling the user's Assistant how to carry out one workflow step by step in plain words.
The user's own Claude Code, which operates the Project through the adops MCP tools and does the Git and Docker work itself.

One of the eleven tools the `adops mcp` server registers (run, preview, validate, edit_file, read_file, list_files, project_view, read_logs, test_connection, accept_schema, drop_branch), which accept only dev or a Branch Environment.
A step in which a Skill confirms Docker is installed and running, ports are free, .env is filled, and git and gh are installed and logged in, before it does anything else.
A per-Git-branch set of br_<branch>__ schemas in the stage Warehouse, run with the run/preview `branch` argument and removed with drop_branch after merge.
A dropped or retyped Source column that halts the affected Step and every later Step until it is accepted.
The `pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml` file that dev accept_schema writes and the Skill commits in a Pull Request, so stage, prod and Branch Environments accept the Breaking Change through Git.
Moving a reviewed change from a Branch Environment to stage on merge and to prod on release through the generated GitHub Actions. Skills explain it but never run it.

phases.name: Add the setup Skill and the Skill checks
phases.goal: `adops init` and `adops init --demo` write `.claude/skills/adops-setup/SKILL.md` into the new Project. A new test module checks every shipped Skill's structure: front matter, MCP tool names, the never-stage-or-prod rule, and that the demo and plain copies are the same.
phases.rationale: A Skill is a Markdown file (SKILL.md) that Claude Code reads from `.claude/skills/<name>/`. It tells the user's Assistant how to carry out one workflow in plain words. Every later Skill relies on the same checks, so the test module is built here together with the first Skill and proves it against a real file. adops-setup comes first because every other Skill assumes its Prerequisite check (Docker, ports, .env, git, gh) has passed. The init code already copies dot-folders as they are (`_copy_tree` in src/adops/interface/init_command.py), so no production code changes.
changes: Write adops-setup/SKILL.md with YAML front matter: `name: adops-setup`, plus a `description` that says when to use it (first-time setup of a new adops Project, or when Docker or the database won't start).

In the body, write numbered steps in plain words. Each step says what it checks and why. (1) Check Docker is installed (`docker --version`) and running (`docker info`). (2) Read the port variables from `.env`, or from `.env.example` if `.env` is missing, and check that nothing is already using those ports. Never hard-code port numbers. (3) If `.env` is missing, copy `.env.example` to `.env` with the shell, then ask the user to fill in the secret values. Say that the MCP `edit_file` tool cannot edit `.env`. (4) Check that git and gh are installed and that `gh auth status` shows a logged-in user. (5) If the folder is not a git repository, run `git init -b main`. (6) Run `docker compose up --wait`. (7) Call `mcp__adops__test_connection` with environment "dev" and `mcp__adops__validate`, and explain the results.

State in the Skill that a plain Project's dev Warehouse (localhost:5432) does not come from docker compose, so the user must provide it. Never tell the user to re-run `adops init` (init refuses a folder that is not empty).

Make the plain copy a byte-identical copy of the demo file. Write the text so it works in both templates: the Skill reads `adops.yaml` and `.env.example` at run time and never assumes demo-only files.

Create tests/unit/interface/test_assistant_skills.py. It finds Skills by globbing `src/adops/templates/{demo,plain}/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and runs every check once per Skill (pytest parametrization).
Add a test that the set of shipped Skill folder names equals a module constant EXPECTED_SKILLS. Set it to {"adops-setup"} for now; later phases add names.
Add a test that demo and plain have the same Skill folders and that each pair of SKILL.md files is byte-identical.
Add a front-matter test. The file starts with a `---` block; parse it with `yaml.safe_load` and assert that `name` equals the folder name and that `description` is a non-empty string.

Add a tool-name test. In the Skill text, an MCP tool is written as a backticked `mcp__adops__<tool>`. Collect every such name and assert each one is in the names returned by `build_server(project)` plus `list_tools()`. Build the project with `write_project` from tests/unit/interface/mcp_harness.py. Do not keep a second hard-coded list of all tools. Also fail on a backticked hyphenated form such as `read-logs`, and on any `mcp__<other>__` prefix.
Add a per-Skill scope test: a dict REQUIRED_TOOLS from Skill name to the tools that Skill must mention. For now it holds adops-setup -> {test_connection, validate}.

Add a never-stage-or-prod test using one module-level list of regexes over call and command patterns: environment set to "stage" or "prod" (`=` or `:`), `--env stage|prod`, `run --all`, `gh release`, and `gh workflow run`. Prose mentions of stage and prod remain allowed. Also add a self-test that runs the regex list over a few known-bad sample lines and asserts each one is caught, so the rule cannot pass when it matches nothing.

In tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py, add `.claude/skills/adops-setup/SKILL.md` to DEMO_FILES. Add `.claude`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills/adops-setup` and the SKILL.md path to the exact listing that the plain-init test expects.
In .github/workflows/ci.yml, step 'Project templates ship in the wheel': add `.claude/skills/adops-setup/SKILL.md` to the demo loop and `plain/.claude/skills/adops-setup/SKILL.md` to the second loop.

Add a **Skill** entry to GLOSSARY.md under Actors, next to Assistant: a SKILL.md file that `adops init` writes to `.claude/skills/<name>/` and that tells the Assistant how to carry out one workflow step by step in plain words. _Avoid_: playbook, prompt.

Write the never-stage-or-prod and forbidden-git-command patterns so they match commands, not prohibitions: Skills phrase warnings without quoting the banned command (e.g. 'stage only the named folders, never everything at once'), and the self-test includes known-good warning and explanation lines (e.g. 'merging sends the change to stage') that must NOT be caught, next to the known-bad lines that must be caught.

rubric.label: Skill checks fail on bad Skills, not just pass on good ones
rubric.ruleStatement: tests/unit/interface/test_assistant_skills.py must find Skills by glob, parametrize per Skill, and actually catch each class of violation: front matter mismatch, unknown or hyphenated or foreign-prefixed MCP tool names, and stage/prod-targeting commands, while letting prose warnings through. 10 = every check is proven by a self-test with both caught-bad and allowed-good lines and no reviewer could find a bypass; 8 = competent and complete; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: `uv run pytest tests/unit/interface/test_assistant_skills.py -v` passes and shows test IDs parametrized per Skill path (demo and plain) for front matter, tool names, required tools and never-stage-or-prod.

phases.goal: Init writes adops-share and adops-promote. adops-share puts a change on a branch, opens a Pull Request and runs its Branch Environment. adops-promote, after the merge, drops the Branch Environment and explains that a merge goes to stage and a release goes to prod.
phases.rationale: Sharing a change and promoting it are the two ends of one Git journey. Both need a stage Environment, which a plain Project does not have, and both must explain Promotion without ever performing it. Reviewing them together keeps that shared rule consistent. phases.name: Add the Skill for accepting a Breaking Change
phases.goal: Init writes adops-breaking-change. It accepts a Breaking Change in dev with accept_schema, commits the accepted-change record at the returned record_path on a branch, and opens the Pull Request that carries the record to stage and prod.
phases.rationale: A Breaking Change (a dropped or retyped Source column) halts a Pipeline until someone accepts it. Stage and prod accept it only when its accepted-change record file arrives through a reviewed Pull Request. Getting the order wrong (committing on main, or skipping the branch) would let the change reach stage unreviewed, so this Skill gets its own reviewed phase.
changes: Write adops-breaking-change/SKILL.md. Explain in plain words what a Breaking Change is and what accepting it means (adops stops expecting the dropped or old-typed column). Ask the user to confirm before accepting.

Handle a reply where `record_path` is null: nothing new needs committing because the files listed in `covered_by` already cover the change. Check those files with `git status` or `git log`, and commit them on the branch if they were never committed.
For a Branch Environment, tell the user to run `adops accept-schema --branch <name>` themselves. Never suggest `--env stage` or `--env prod`.
Make the plain copy byte-identical to the demo copy. Write it so that a missing `pipelines/accepted/` folder (plain Project) is fine, because accept_schema creates it.

rubric.label: Pull Request step explains how stage and prod accept
rubric.ruleStatement: After committing, the Skill must push and `gh pr create`, and explain in plain words that merging this Pull Request lets stage, and later prod, accept the change — without performing or quoting any Promotion command. 10 = the user understands why the PR matters; 8 = expected; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: `git push -u origin <name>` and `gh pr create` appear after the commit (`grep -n`).
A sentence explains merge -> stage accepts, release -> prod accepts, in prose.
The never-stage-or-prod test passes for this Skill.
`cmp` demo vs plain reports no difference; EXPECTED_SKILLS has all six names; ci.yml lists both new paths.
failureExamples: Plausible: the Skill opens the PR but never says why, so the user merges an unrelated PR first and is surprised stage still halts.
The Skill suggests running accept-schema on stage by hand to 'speed it up'.

phases.healerHint: Most likely the null record_path case is missing or the branch is created after accept_schema; move `git checkout -b` above the accept step and add a short record_path-null paragraph that checks the covered_by files with git status.

phases.name: Test the share and Breaking Change Git steps
phases.goal: One test without Docker or an LLM replays the Git steps of adops-share and adops-breaking-change on a demo Project, pushes both branches to a local bare repository, and proves that only the named paths were committed and that the branch carrying the accepted-change record passes `adops validate`.
phases.rationale: The structural tests check the Skill text but not whether the Git steps it describes actually work. This test runs the same commands the Skills tell the Assistant to run, against a real git repository, so a wrong command order or a missing record fails CI. It lives in tests/unit because unit tests already run git, and it uses a hand-written record instead of a live accept_schema run. That keeps Docker and the 20-minute end-to-end budget out of it.
changes: Create tests/unit/interface/test_skill_git_steps.py. Reuse the hermetic GIT_ENV and git(*args, cwd) pattern from test_init_command.py (lines 292-300), either by importing it or by moving it into a shared helper in tests/unit/interface/ if importing a test module is awkward.

Steps: run `adops init --demo` into tmp_path; `git init -b main`; commit everything as the initial commit; `git checkout -b accept-orders`; write a prepared record `pipelines/accepted/20261123T000000Z-shop_sync-orders.yaml` with `{pipeline: shop_sync, table: orders, changes: ['customer_id dropped']}`, using a column that really exists in the demo Source; `git add` only that named path; commit; create a bare repo with `git init --bare`; add it as origin; `git push -u origin accept-orders`.

Before the record, replay adops-share's own steps: on branch share-change edit a Pipeline file under pipelines/, `git add` only the named paths (pipelines/, dbt/, adops.yaml), commit and push; assert the pushed commit touches only those paths and that .env and .adops/ are absent even though both exist in the working folder.
Clone the bare repo at branch accept-orders into a new folder. Assert that the record file is present and byte-equal to what was written, and that `.env` and `.adops/` are not in the clone.
Run validate on the clone (the CLI's validate command, via typer CliRunner or `validate_project`) and assert that it passes with no problems.

Tie the replay to the Skill text: assert the shipped adops-share and adops-breaking-change SKILL.md files contain the replayed commands (`git checkout -b`, `git add`, `git commit`, `git push -u origin`, `gh pr create`) in the same order the test runs them, so a Skill that reorders or drops a step fails.
inputs: Phase add-share-and-promote-skills: shipped adops-share SKILL.md
Phase add-breaking-change-skill: shipped adops-breaking-change SKILL.md
Discovery: git already used in unit tests with GIT_ENV helper (test_init_command.py:292-300,706-740)
Discovery: adops validate checks records offline (validate_command.py:58-117)
phases.expectedResult: `uv run pytest tests/unit/interface/test_skill_git_steps.py` passes offline, with no Docker and no network, proving the share and Breaking Change Git steps (in the Skills' own order) push only named paths and a record that passes `adops validate`.
guardNotes: g1: the new test file stays within ruff rules and 100 columns.
g2: no src/adops code changes; the test only adds coverage.
g4: the replay lives in tests/unit, not tests/e2e, so it adds nothing to the Docker end-to-end job or its 20-minute timeout.

rubric.label: Replay runs real git against a local bare repo, offline
rubric.ruleStatement: tests/unit/interface/test_skill_git_steps.py must run `adops init --demo`, real git commands (init, checkout -b, add named paths, commit, push -u origin) against a `git init --bare` origin in tmp_path, with the hermetic GIT_ENV, and no Docker, network or LLM. 10 = fully hermetic and deterministic; 8 = expected; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: `uv run pytest tests/unit/interface/test_skill_git_steps.py -v` passes with network disabled and Docker stopped.
The test uses a GIT_ENV/git(*args, cwd) helper (imported or shared under tests/unit/interface/), not the developer's global git config.
Both branches (share-change and accept-orders) are pushed with `git push -u origin` to a `git init --bare` repo under tmp_path.
No `gh` command is executed (gh pr create is only checked in Skill text).
The file is under tests/unit/ (not tests/e2e/) and `git diff --stat HEAD -- src/adops` is empty.
failureExamples: Plausible: the test monkeypatches subprocess and asserts command strings, so it never proves the git steps actually work.
The test relies on the developer's ~/.gitconfig user.name and fails in CI.
The test calls `gh pr create` and needs network.

rubric.label: Pushed commits contain only named paths
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must prove that what arrives in the remote contains only the named paths: the share commit touches only pipelines/, dbt/, adops.yaml, the record commit touches only the record file, and .env and .adops/ are absent from the clone even though both exist in the working folder. 10 = asserted on the pushed commit and on a fresh clone; 8 = expected; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: The test creates `.env` and `.adops/` in the working folder before staging (assert they exist).
It asserts the share commit's changed files (e.g. `git show --name-only` or `git diff-tree`) are all under pipelines/, dbt/ or adops.yaml.
It clones the bare repo at accept-orders into a new folder and asserts the record file is byte-equal to what was written and `.env`/.adops/ are absent.
It asserts the accept-orders commit changed exactly the one record path.
failureExamples: Plausible: the test never creates .env in the working folder (init does not write one), so 'absent from clone' passes trivially.
Asserts only that the record exists in the clone, not that nothing else was committed.
Checks the local branch instead of the cloned remote, so a failed push is not detected.

rubric.label: The pushed record passes adops validate
rubric.ruleStatement: The hand-written record must use a real demo Pipeline, table and column, and validate (CLI via CliRunner or validate_project) on the clone must pass with no problems. 10 = also proves validate would fail on a bad record; 8 = passes on the real record; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: The record is `pipelines/accepted/20261123T000000Z-shop_sync-orders.yaml` with pipeline shop_sync, table orders, and a column that exists in the demo Source (check with `grep -rn customer_id src/adops/templates/demo`).
validate runs against the clone folder, not the working folder, and the test asserts exit code 0 / no problems.
Optional strength: a negative assertion that a record naming a non-existent Pipeline makes validate report a problem.
failureExamples: Plausible: validate runs on the original working folder, so a missing record in the push is not caught.
The record uses a column name that is not in the demo Source and validate is not checked for problems, only for not raising.

rubric.label: Replay order is checked against the shipped Skill text
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must assert that the shipped adops-share and adops-breaking-change SKILL.md files contain `git checkout -b`, `git add`, `git commit`, `git push -u origin`, `gh pr create` in the same order the test runs them, so reordering or dropping a step in a Skill fails. 10 = order derived from one shared sequence used by both replay and assertion; 8 = expected; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: The test reads both SKILL.md files from src/adops/templates/demo/.claude/skills/ and checks index order of the five commands.
Swapping `git commit` above `git checkout -b` in a scratch copy of adops-share makes the test fail.
The command sequence is defined once in the test and used for both the replay description and the order assertion.
failureExamples: Plausible: the test only checks each command is present (`in text`), so a Skill that commits before branching still passes.
Order is checked in adops-share only; adops-breaking-change is not read.

phases.healerHint: The likeliest gap is a vacuous 'secrets absent' check because init writes no .env; create .env and .adops/ in the working folder before staging and assert on a fresh clone of the bare repo, not the local branch.

successCriteria: Done and correct when ALL of these hold. (1) The demo and plain templates ship exactly six files, `.claude/skills/{adops-setup,adops-build,adops-test-in-dev,adops-share,adops-breaking-change,adops-promote}/SKILL.md`. `adops init` and `adops init --demo` write all six into the new Project, and no tool code is copied. The CI step that checks templates ship in the wheel lists all 12 new template paths. (2) Each SKILL.md has valid YAML front matter: `name` equals its folder name, and `description` is non-empty and says when to use the Skill. (3) Each Skill covers its confirmed scope. adops-setup checks that Docker is installed and running, the compose ports are free, `.env` is filled from `.env.example`, and git and gh are installed and logged in, then starts `docker compose up`. adops-build uses list_files, read_file, project_view, edit_file and validate. adops-test-in-dev uses run, preview, read_logs and test_connection, and explains failures plainly. adops-share creates a branch, commits, pushes, opens a Pull Request with `gh pr create`, and runs the Branch Environment with run/preview `branch=`. adops-breaking-change calls accept_schema in dev, then commits the file at the returned `record_path` under `pipelines/accepted/` on a branch and opens the Pull Request that carries the record. adops-promote, after the merge, calls drop_branch and explains that a merge goes to stage and a release goes to prod. (4) Unit tests, at the repo's 100% line+branch coverage, assert for every Skill that the front matter is valid, that every MCP tool name it mentions is a tool `build_server` really registers (run, preview, validate, drop_branch, accept_schema, project_view, list_files, read_file, edit_file, read_logs, test_connection), and that it never targets stage or prod: no MCP call or adops command passes environment/--env stage or prod, and no Skill runs `adops run --all`, a release or a prod workflow. (5) One E2E test, with no LLM, replays the Git steps of adops-share and adops-breaking-change on a demo Project: git init, create a branch, run dev accept_schema (or a prepared record) to produce `pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml`, commit it, and push to a local bare repo. It asserts the pushed branch holds the record and passes `adops validate`. (6) All existing repo gates stay green: lint, types, 100% coverage, unit job and Docker E2E inside the 20-minute CI budget. No test needs an LLM key.

deferred: Running or evaluating a real Assistant (Claude Code or any LLM) against the Skills: v1 needs no LLM key (vision item 12), and the user set the quality bar to structural tests plus one Git-replay E2E.
Skills for other Assistants (AGENTS.md, Cursor rules, Codex): the user confirmed Claude Code only, consistent with the horizon-9 .mcp.json-only decision.
New or changed MCP tools, including any Git tool inside the MCP server: the horizon-9 decision keeps Git out of the server, so the Skills do Git through the Assistant's shell.

Running stage or prod, `adops run --all`, publishing releases or triggering Promotion workflows from a Skill: ADR-0014 and the horizon-9 allow-list keep the Assistant in dev and Branch Environments. adops-promote only explains this.
Proving Promotion on a real self-hosted runner, or changing the generated GitHub Actions workflows: that is MAP candidate #16.
Adding a dbt project to the plain template: that is MAP candidate #17. Skills only work with whatever dbt/ exists.
Fixing the MCP tool-call timeout for long runs and the `dbt/profiles.yml` dev-redirect gap: that is MAP candidate #18, whose timeout half needs real use of these Skills first.
Calling GitHub or gh in tests (real PR creation, gh auth): tests must stay offline and deterministic, so the E2E stops at a push to a local bare repo.
Automating drop-branch on PR merge or close in CI: horizon 6 made drop-branch manual, and adops-promote calls the MCP drop_branch tool by hand.
An upgrade command that adds Skills to existing Projects: init refuses non-empty folders, and an upgrade path is new CLI surface that nobody requested.
Environments/Promotion and single-VM playbooks: those are vision item 11 and MAP #19. The Skills explain steps inline but are not the playbooks.
An analytics `/ask` Skill: ADR-0010 defers the Analytics Agent and its skill to v1.1.
